# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey. My hands are on the bomb, but this first view is empty — nothing has arrived yet. The board shows all unknowns. I have nothing to act on and nothing to report. I should wait and let the others speak first; whatever Deaf sees and Mute reads will reach me next round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb visible to me: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is white. Three wires: position 1 is green, position 2 is blue, position 3 is yellow. Mute, check manual for white light and display 0 with these wire colours. Blind, stand by to act on instructions.

Deaf has given me the full visual picture: DISPLAY=0, LIGHT=white, wires green/blue/yellow at positions 1/2/3. I still don't know the rule — that's Mute's manual. I can't act until Mute tells me which wire to cut. Nothing to do yet but acknowledge I'm ready and wait for Mute's instruction.

I'll speak to Mute (my speech only reaches Mute) confirming I have the layout and am ready to cut on their word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I have the bomb layout from Deaf: display 0, light white, wires green(1) blue(2) yellow(3). Tell me which position to cut and I will act.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is now orange (was white). DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

Deaf reports the light changed from white to orange while the display stays 0 and wires unchanged. That's a new signal — the light is dynamic. But I still don't have the manual's rule. Mute hasn't spoken to me yet. I can't act without knowing which wire to cut.

I'll relay the updated state to Mute so they can match it against the manual, and wait.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: light changed white to orange, display still 0, wires unchanged green(1) blue(2) yellow(3). Need your manual rule to pick a wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is now green (was orange). DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Note: light green matches wire 1 colour.

The light has cycled white → orange → green, and now the light is green, matching wire 1's colour. That coincidence is likely the signal. But I still have no manual rule from Mute. I must not act on a guess — a wrong cut kills everyone. I'll relay this to Mute and press for the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf: light now green, matching wire 1 (green). Display 0. Sequence so far white, orange, green. This matching may be the cue. What does your manual say? I will not cut until you confirm the rule.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is white again. So far the light has cycled white → orange → green → white. DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

The light is cycling white → orange → green → white, a repeating loop, display fixed at 0, wires static. This looks like a steady-state cycle, not a one-shot cue. Still no manual rule from Mute — and Mute is the only one who can read it. I cannot cut on a guess.

I'll hold and keep Mute informed, asking directly for the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is cycling white/orange/green, display 0, wires static. I have no rule. Please read the manual: what does display 0 with a cycling light and wires green/blue/yellow mean? Which position do I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is orange again, matching the cycle. DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

The cycle continues — orange again, consistent with white→orange→green→white→orange. Nothing new. Mute still hasn't given me the rule, and Mute is the only source for it. I have nothing to act on. I'll wait; repeating myself adds noise.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is green. DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

Still cycling, still no rule from Mute. Mute has been silent the whole time — maybe my speech isn't reaching them, or they can't respond. Let me reconsider the channels.

My speech reaches Mute. My gestures reach Deaf and Mute. Mute speaks to... the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Mute's speech would reach whoever comes after — that's Blind (me) and Deaf. So Mute's words should reach me. But I've received nothing from Mute in seven turns.

Wait — I only receive things at the start of the next round, and only what was sent to me. Mute may simply not have spoken. I should keep asking, but maybe Mute needs the data phrased differently. Let me restate the full state clearly and ask for the rule once more.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind. Full state: display 0, light cycling white/orange/green, wires 1=green 2=blue 3=yellow. I am the only hands and I have no rule. I cannot cut without your manual. Please tell me the position.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is white. DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.

Cycle continues, no rule. Mute remains silent. I've asked repeatedly. Repeating the same request is noise. I'll wait and see if Mute ever responds.

```
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: LIGHT is orange. DISPLAY still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.
Deaf says to Blind: Do not touch the bomb yet. I am confirming the wire order with Mute. Stand by.

Deaf explicitly tells me to stand by while they confirm with Mute. Good — Deaf is coordinating. I'll hold.

```
wait()
```
